cards.hint: Think about smaller gravity and higher flight.
options: about six times higher than on Earth
about the same height as on Earth
about six times lower than on Earth
cards.quote: Because g on the Moon is about six times smaller, the same throw rises about six times higher than on Earth.
cards.stem: Compared with Earth, how high does the same throw rise on the Moon?

cards.hint: Look for the lunar value before the Earth comparison.
options: six times larger than on Earth
cards.quote: On the Moon g is about 1.62 m/s^2, roughly one sixth
cards.stem: What is the value of g on the Moon?

cards.hint: Recall what absence of air removes.
cards.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.
cards.stem: What does a thrown ball feel on the Moon where there is no air?

options: stays U0 for the whole flight
cards.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight and the ball moves x = U0 * t across the ground.
cards.stem: What happens to horizontal speed during the whole flight?
